marks.gloss_en: read from the baraita's wording: it says one does not place an 'eruv' in it -- the eruv of courtyards, not the shituf
what is the reason [for the eruv clauses]? because it is not fit for dwelling
דתנן: עירובי חצרות בחצר, שיתופי מבוי במבוי -- the shituf goes in a courtyard of the alleyway
what is the reason? because it is no worse than a courtyard in the alleyway
והאי לא גרע מחצר שבמבוי -- on the emended mishnah, the shituf goes in a courtyard of the alleyway, and this house is no worse
אלא אימא: עירובי חצרות בבית שבחצר, ושיתופי מבואות בחצר שבמבוי (= p_eima_bayit_shebechatzer)
rather say: the eruv of courtyards [is placed] in a house in the courtyard, and the shituf of alleyways in a courtyard in the alleyway
דאמר רב הונא: חצר לפי פתחיה מתחלקת
ורב חסדא אמר: נותן לכל פתח ופתח ארבע אמות
rather say: it has no law of division like a courtyard
והוינן בה: עירובי חצרות בחצר? והתנן: הנותן עירובו בבית שער אכסדרה ומרפסת — אינו עירוב
one who places his eruv in a gatehouse, a portico or a balcony -- it is no eruv; and one who lives there does not prohibit [the courtyard]
והתנן: אין חולקין את החצר עד שיהא בה ארבע אמות לזה וארבע אמות לזה -- unanswered; the stam abandons the diyuk and re-reads the baraita (3b.11)
one does not divide the courtyard unless it has four amot for this one and four amot for that one
and one does not make it an extension [ibur] between two towns
what is the reason? because 'house' is written in all of them
for we do not treat it even like watchmen's huts [burganin]
the reason is that it lacks four amot; but if it has four amot, they divide it
that applies to a house which stands to endure -- we give it courtyard; this, which stands to be torn down -- we do not give it courtyard
a sukkah above twenty amot lowered by cushions and blankets: it is not a diminution
